The announcement doesn't mention bridging, so that finding stands, and we haven't re-read the rest of Kuma's site since 6 October.
Kuma's announcement
Kuma's connection to Stoat:

“For obvious reasons, as I work much closer to the wonderful Stoat Team, it is clear that I can no longer maintain a direct line between Stoat and Kuma on some levels. […] I am staying on as a maintainer; however, I will be stepping back from Platform Compliance entirely. […] I will no longer oversee platform compliance in order to eliminate any conflict of interest as much as possible.”
Aki, Kuma's developer, in a message on Stoat · October 2026

We welcome Kuma separating its compliance work from its developer's role at Stoat. It also shows why public rules matter: when a bot's developer works closely with the platform, users and other developers need to be able to see that the same requirements apply.
What Stoat told us about the same practices:
“Having cross-server processing cannot be used to create a general profile for users across unrelated community servers.”
“Removing the raw IP address data from the equation does not in itself resolve the core concern if a fingerprint continues to function as a persistent identifier.”

We removed cross-server alerts and IP checks to meet these requirements. When we read Kuma's website on 6 October it described both, switched on by default, and Kuma has since removed them from its Stoat verification. Its bridging, as we read it then, sends members' messages to other platforms on an admin's decision alone. If the same standard applies to every bot, Stoat should say so publicly. If it doesn't, it should explain what makes the cases different.

We're glad developer guidelines are on the way, and we'll update this page when they're published. Until then there's no timeline.
Stoat's latest guidance
bronx's developer asked Stoat Trust & Safety a detailed set of questions and shared the answers with us on 10 October 2026. We've summarised each question and quoted Stoat's answer.
What this means:

Stoat is currently asking every bot to use opt-in for data tied to a person, including per-person stats and rankings. Message content and attachments should be kept for 30 days unless there's a specific reason, such as a case under appeal, which is the schedule Stoatmod already uses. Other operational data can be kept while it's needed. Privacy policies will become a requirement, with a migration period once the guidelines are published. Stoat hasn't decided on bridge bots yet.
